newsitem.title: IRAQ: IRAQ ATTACKS LEBANON OVER ARAB GAMES' EXCLUSION.
newsitem.headline: IRAQ ATTACKS LEBANON OVER ARAB GAMES' EXCLUSION.

text.p: Iraqi newspapers on Sunday harshly attacked Lebanon for its refusal to allowi Iraqi athletes to attend the Pan Arab Games in Beirut after pressure from Kuwait and Saudi Arabia.
Iraq's most influential newspaper Babel said in a front-page editorial that Lebanon had prevented the athletes from entering Lebanon "for silly financial profits..."

Kuwait and Saudi Arabia, Gulf War foes of Iraq, are among the most generous Arab financiers of Lebanon's postwar reconstruction and the main contributors to the $50 million cost of the new sports stadium where the games opened on Saturday.
They threatened to boycott the games if Iraq competed, a Lebanese official said on Wednesday.
The 97 Iraqi athletes, stranded for two days at the Lebanese border, headed home on Saturday after Beirut refused to grant them visas to take part in the games.

Babel, owned by President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday, said, ... "such a decision will not effect Iraq's prestige but it contains (implicit) condemnation of the rulers of Kuwait and Saudi Arabia."
Iraq is blaming the Lebanese decision excluding Iraq from the games on Kuwait and Saudi Arabia.
Al-Thawra, newspaper of the ruling Baath party, said: "Our expectation has come true...We are living in a bad time governed by illgotten finance."
"It is dishonourable for us to attend such a sports gathering full of hatred and hostility," the paper added.
The paper also criticised the Arab League Secretary-General Esmat Abdel-Meguid, saying he had done nothing to allow Iraqis attend the games. It accused him of not "shouldering his esponsibility."
The Pan Arab Games, which are held every four years, are the first major international event staged in the Lebanese capital since the end of the 1975-90 civil war.
